solution:
## Write profit as revenue minus pay-out
Let $x$ be the charge per play in euro. Average pay-out per play is $\text{€}2.29$.
600 &= 845(x - 2.29)
## Solve for x
\frac{600}{845} &= x - 2.29
x &= \frac{600}{845} + 2.29
x &\approx 0.71 + 2.29
x &= 3.00
ANSWER: \text{€}3.00

## Identify the triangle BCD and its sides
$A$ is the midpoint of both diagonals and $BA$ is vertical, so $|BD| = |BC| = 3$. Also $|CD| = 2.5$.
Let $\alpha = \angle BCD$. It is opposite the side $BD$.
## Write the cosine rule
Below, $c$ stands for $\cos\alpha$.
|BD|^2 &= |BC|^2 + |CD|^2 - 2|BC||CD|\cos\alpha
3^2 &= 3^2 + 2.5^2 - 2(3)(2.5)\cos\alpha
9 &= 9 + 6.25 - 15\cos\alpha
9 &= 15.25 - 15\cos\alpha
## Solve for cos α
15\cos\alpha &= 15.25 - 9
15\cos\alpha &= 6.25
\cos\alpha &= \frac{6.25}{15}
&= \frac{1.25}{3}
## Find the angle
\alpha &= \cos^{-1}\!\left(\frac{1.25}{3}\right)
&\approx 65.4^\circ
&\approx 65^\circ
ANSWER: \angle BCD = 65^\circ

## Identify the four triangular faces
Faces $BCD$ and $BEF$ are isosceles with sides $3, 3, 2.5$. The angle between the sides $2.5$ and $3$ is $\angle BCD = 65^\circ$.
Faces $BCF$ and $BDE$ are equilateral with all sides $3$ (each has $|BC| = |CF| = |BF| = 3$), so each angle is $60^\circ$.
Use area $= \tfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C$ for each pair.
## Total area of the four faces
A &= 2\left[\tfrac{1}{2}(2.5)(3)\sin 65^\circ\right] + 2\left[\tfrac{1}{2}(3)(3)\sin 60^\circ\right]
&= 2(3.75)(0.9063) + 2(4.5)(0.8660)
&= 6.797 + 7.794
&= 14.59
&\approx 15\text{ m}^2
ANSWER: 15\text{ m}^2

## Plot the nine points from the table
Plot $(t, h)$ using time on the horizontal axis and height on the vertical axis.
The points are $(0, 3.1)$, $(3, 1.6)$, $(6, 0.1)$, $(9, 1.6)$, $(12, 3.1)$, $(15, 1.6)$, $(18, 0.1)$, $(21, 1.6)$, $(24, 3.1)$.
## Join the points with a smooth curve
It is a cosine wave: maximum $3.1$ at midnight, midday and the next midnight, minimum $0.1$ at 6 a.m. and 6 p.m. It crosses $1.6$ at 3 a.m., 9 a.m., 3 p.m. and 9 p.m.
ANSWER: \text{Cosine curve through the nine points}

## Find when the loaded barge can enter
Loaded, it needs at least $2$ m. Draw the line $h = 2$ on the graph. The rising curve meets it at about 9:30 a.m. on the curve from (d)(ii), so the barge enters then.
## Find when the unloaded barge must leave
Unloaded, it needs at least $1.5$ m. Draw the line $h = 1.5$. The falling curve meets it at about 15:08 (3:08 p.m.) on our curve, so the barge must leave before then. The marking scheme read 9:30 and 15:15 (5 h 45 min); readings close to the curve are accepted.
## Subtract the times
15{:}08 - 9{:}30 &= 5\text{ h }38\text{ min}
ANSWER: \approx 5\text{ h }38\text{ min}

## Standardise the income €60 000
Here $\mu = \text{€}39\,400$ and $\sigma = \text{€}12\,920$. Use $z = \dfrac{x - \mu}{\sigma}$.
z &= \frac{60000 - 39400}{12920}
&= \frac{20600}{12920}
&\approx 1.59
## Find the probability above this z-value
From the tables, $P(z < 1.59) = 0.9441$.
P(z > 1.59) &= 1 - P(z < 1.59)
&= 1 - 0.9441
&= 0.0559
&= 5.59\%
&\approx 5.6\%
ANSWER: 5.6\%

## Find the z-value for the lowest 10%
The tables give $P(z \le 1.28) = 0.9$. By symmetry the value with $10\%$ below it is $z = -1.28$.
## Convert back to an income
\frac{x - 39400}{12920} &= -1.28
x - 39400 &= -1.28(12920)
x - 39400 &= -16537.6
x &= 39400 - 16537.6
x &= 22862.4
x &\approx \text{€}22\,862
ANSWER: \text{€}22\,862

## State the hypotheses
The population mean was $\text{€}39\,400$. We test whether it has changed (either direction), so the test is two-tailed.
H_0:\ \mu &= 39400
H_1:\ \mu &\ne 39400
## Calculate the test statistic
The sample has $n = 1000$ and $\bar{x} = 38\,280$; $\sigma = 12\,920$.
z &= \frac{\bar{x} - \mu}{\sigma/\sqrt{n}}
&= \frac{38280 - 39400}{12920/\sqrt{1000}}
&= \frac{-1120}{12920/\sqrt{1000}}
&= \frac{-1120}{408.57}
&\approx -2.74
## Compare with the 5% critical values
At the $5\%$ level, two-tailed, the critical values are $\pm 1.96$.
-2.74 &< -1.96
## Write the conclusion
$z$ lies outside $[-1.96, 1.96]$, so the result is significant. Reject $H_0$.
There is evidence that the mean annual income of full-time workers has changed since the national data were published.
ANSWER: z = -2.74 < -1.96\text{, so reject } H_0\text{: the mean income has changed}

## Write the 95% confidence interval
Use $\bar{x} \pm 1.96\dfrac{s}{\sqrt{n}}$ with $\bar{x} = 26\,974$, $s = 5120$ and $n = 400$.
\text{Interval} &= 26974 \pm 1.96\left(\frac{5120}{\sqrt{400}}\right)
## Work out the margin of error
E &= 1.96\left(\frac{5120}{\sqrt{400}}\right)
&= 1.96\left(\frac{5120}{20}\right)
&= 1.96 \times 256
&= 501.76
## Find the two ends of the interval
\text{Lower} &= 26974 - 501.76
&= 26472.24
\text{Upper} &= 26974 + 501.76
&= 27475.76
ANSWER: 26472.24 \le \mu \le 27475.76

## Give a reason
Farm size is not normally distributed, but the sampling distribution of the sample means from many large samples will be approximately normal (central limit theorem).
So normal-distribution methods, such as confidence intervals, can be used for the mean farm size.
ANSWER: \text{The distribution of sample means will be normally distributed.}

## Set the margin of error equal to 4.5%
The margin of error is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$, and $4.5\% = 0.045$.
\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} &= 0.045
## Solve for n
\sqrt{n} &= \frac{1}{0.045}
n &= \left(\frac{1}{0.045}\right)^2
&= 493.8
&\approx 494
ANSWER: n = 494

## Find the pay for the deliveries
She is paid $\text{€}2$ for each of her 5 deliveries.
5 \times \text{€}2 &= \text{€}10
## Subtract this from the total pay
What is left is the pay for the 2 hours worked.
\text{€}28 - \text{€}10 &= \text{€}18
## Divide by the 2 hours
\text{€}18 \div 2 &= \text{€}9
ANSWER: \text{€}9 \text{ per hour}

## Write the pay for the hours
The hourly rate is $\text{€}9$, so $h$ hours pay:
\text{Hours pay} &= 9h
## Write the pay for the deliveries
Each delivery pays $\text{€}2$, so $d$ deliveries pay:
\text{Delivery pay} &= 2d
## Add the two amounts
w &= 9h + 2d
ANSWER: w = 9h + 2d

## Pay for the 6 weekday hours
6 \times 9 &= 54
## Pay for the 12 weekday deliveries
12 \times 2 &= 24
## Find the Sunday hourly rate
Time and a half means $1.5$ times the normal rate.
9 \times 1.5 &= 13.5
## Pay for the 5 Sunday hours
5 \times 13.5 &= 67.5
## Write an equation for the total pay
Let $d$ be the number of Sunday deliveries, paid $\text{€}2$ each.
54 + 24 + 67.5 + 2d &= 161.5
78 + 67.5 + 2d &= 161.5
145.5 + 2d &= 161.5
## Solve for d
2d &= 161.5 - 145.5
2d &= 16
d &= 8
ANSWER: d = 8 \text{ deliveries}

## Substitute z₁ and z₂
z_3 &= z_1 + 2z_2
&= (1 + 3i) + 2(2 - i)
## Multiply out the bracket
&= 1 + 3i + 4 - 2i
## Collect real and imaginary parts
&= 5 + i
ANSWER: z_3 = 5 + i

## Write each number as a point (Re, Im)
$z_1 = 1 + 3i$ is the point $(1, 3)$.
$z_2 = 2 - i$ is the point $(2, -1)$.
$z_3 = 5 + i$ is the point $(5, 1)$.
## Plot and label the points
The real part is read along the Re axis and the imaginary part up the Im axis.
ANSWER: z_1 = (1, 3),\; z_2 = (2, -1),\; z_3 = (5, 1)

## Write w as a fraction
w &= \frac{z_1}{z_2}
&= \frac{1 + 3i}{2 - i}
## Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate of 2 − i
The conjugate of $2 - i$ is $2 + i$.
&= \frac{(1 + 3i)(2 + i)}{(2 - i)(2 + i)}
## Multiply out the numerator
(1 + 3i)(2 + i) &= 2 + i + 6i + 3i^2
&= 2 + 7i - 3
&= -1 + 7i
## Multiply out the denominator
(2 - i)(2 + i) &= 4 + 2i - 2i - i^2
&= 4 + 1
&= 5
## Divide and write in the form a + bi
w &= \frac{-1 + 7i}{5}
&= -\frac{1}{5} + \frac{7}{5}i
ANSWER: w = -\frac{1}{5} + \frac{7}{5}i

## Multiply out each bracket
3(x - 7) + 5(x - 4) &= 15
3x - 21 + 5x - 20 &= 15
## Collect like terms
8x - 41 &= 15
## Add 41 to both sides
8x &= 15 + 41
8x &= 56
## Divide both sides by 8
x &= 7
ANSWER: x = 7

## Rearrange the second equation
5a &= 25 + 2b
5a - 2b &= 25
Call the equations $4a + 3b = -3$ (1) and $5a - 2b = 25$ (2).
## Multiply (1) by 2
8a + 6b &= -6
## Multiply (2) by 3
15a - 6b &= 75
## Add the two new equations to eliminate b
8a + 6b + 15a - 6b &= -6 + 75
23a &= 69
## Divide both sides by 23
a &= 3
## Substitute a = 3 into (1)
4(3) + 3b &= -3
12 + 3b &= -3
3b &= -15
b &= -5
ANSWER: a = 3,\; b = -5

## Multiply out the bracket
2(2x - 3) + 6x &< 25
4x - 6 + 6x &< 25
## Collect like terms
10x - 6 &< 25
## Add 6 to both sides
10x &< 31
## Divide both sides by 10
x &< 3.1
## List the natural numbers below 3.1
Since $x \in \mathbb{N}$, the values are $1, 2, 3$.
ANSWER: x \in \{1, 2, 3\}

## Put x = 0 (the y-axis)
Any point on the $y$-axis has $x = 0$.
f(0) &= 0^3 + 0^2 - 2(0) + 7
&= 7
ANSWER: (0, 7)

## Substitute x = 1 into f(x)
f(1) &= 1^3 + 1^2 - 2(1) + 7
&= 1 + 1 - 2 + 7
&= 7
## Compare with the point
$f(1) = 7$, so the point $A(1, 7)$ is on the graph of $f$.
ANSWER: f(1) = 7

## Differentiate each term
Use $\frac{d}{dx}(x^n) = nx^{n-1}$; the derivative of a constant is $0$.
f(x) &= x^3 + x^2 - 2x + 7
f'(x) &= 3x^2 + 2x - 2
## Substitute x = 1 to find the slope
f'(1) &= 3(1)^2 + 2(1) - 2
&= 3 + 2 - 2
&= 3
ANSWER: f'(x) = 3x^2 + 2x - 2, \quad \text{slope} = 3

## Use the point and the slope
The slope is $m = 3$ and the point is $(1, 7)$.
y - y_1 &= m(x - x_1)
## Substitute
y - 7 &= 3(x - 1)
## Multiply out the bracket
y - 7 &= 3x - 3
## Add 7 to both sides
y &= 3x + 4
ANSWER: y = 3x + 4

## Find the first differences
Subtract each term from the next one.
15 - 13 &= 2
19 - 15 &= 4
25 - 19 &= 6
33 - 25 &= 8
## Spot the pattern
The first differences are $2, 4, 6, 8$: they go up by $2$ each time, so the next ones are $10, 12, 14$.
## Find U₆
U_6 &= 33 + 10
&= 43
## Find U₇
U_7 &= 43 + 12
&= 55
## Find U₈
U_8 &= 55 + 14
&= 69
## Find the second differences
The first differences are $2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14$. Subtract each from the next one.
4 - 2 &= 2
6 - 4 &= 2
8 - 6 &= 2
10 - 8 &= 2
12 - 10 &= 2
14 - 12 &= 2
## Conclude
The second differences are all $2$ (constant), so the pattern is quadratic.
ANSWER: U_6 = 43,\; U_7 = 55,\; U_8 = 69

## Substitute n = 1
$U_1 = 13$.
1^2 + b(1) + c &= 13
1 + b + c &= 13
b + c &= 12
## Substitute n = 2
$U_2 = 15$.
2^2 + b(2) + c &= 15
4 + 2b + c &= 15
2b + c &= 11
## Subtract the equations to find b
Subtract $b + c = 12$ from $2b + c = 11$.
(2b + c) - (b + c) &= 11 - 12
b &= 11 - 12
b &= -1
## Substitute b = -1 into b + c = 12
-1 + c &= 12
c &= 12 + 1
c &= 13
ANSWER: b = -1,\; c = 13

## Identify a and d
The first term is $a = 12$ and the common difference is $d = 14 - 12 = 2$.
## Write the formula for Tₙ
T_n &= a + (n - 1)d
&= 12 + (n - 1)(2)
&= 12 + 2n - 2
&= 10 + 2n
## Substitute n = 30
T_{30} &= 10 + 2(30)
&= 10 + 60
&= 70
ANSWER: T_n = 10 + 2n, \quad T_{30} = 70

## Find the tax at 20% on the first part
The 20% rate applies to the first $\text{€}1300$.
0.2 \times 1300 &= 260
## Find the amount taxed at 40%
1550 - 1300 &= 250
## Find the tax at 40% on the remainder
0.4 \times 250 &= 100
## Add the two amounts of tax
260 + 100 &= 360
## Subtract the tax credits
360 - 126 &= 234
ANSWER: \text{€}234

## Find the part of her wage taxed at 5.5%
The first $\text{€}462$ and the next $\text{€}214$ are taxed at lower rates; the rest is the balance.
1550 - 462 - 214 &= 874
## USC on the first 462 at 1%
462 \times 0.01 &= 4.62
## USC on the next 214 at 3%
214 \times 0.03 &= 6.42
## USC on the balance of 874 at 5.5%
874 \times 0.055 &= 48.07
## Add the three amounts
4.62 + 6.42 + 48.07 &= 59.11
ANSWER: \text{€}59.11

## Add her three deductions
The deductions are income tax, USC and PRSI.
234 + 59.11 + 18 &= 311.11
## Write the deductions as a percentage of her gross wage
\frac{311.11}{1550} \times 100 &= 20.07\ldots
&\approx 20.1
ANSWER: \text{(i) } \text{€}311.11 \quad \text{(ii) } 20.1\%
